A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ExtGNAN and graph-subset framework, renamed from GMAN to SuperMAN. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions to the medical evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original P12, Crohn’s disease, and GossipCop experiments in Tables 1–3, together with attribution analyses in Figures 2–4.

after.justification: v3 reports medical and GossipCop experiments, component ablations, grouping comparisons, calibration, and noise-robustness results in Tables 1–8 and accompanying figures.

M1.justification: The ExtGNAN, DeepSet aggregation, and additive prediction architecture remain substantially unchanged under renaming. v3 adds a reachability-conditioned distance definition in Section 3 and an optional sparse, adjacent-node masking adaptation in Appendix C. These are limited procedural additions; their use in the reported experiments is not established.

E1.justification: The reported P12 target changes from in-hospital mortality to whether ICU length of stay exceeds 72 hours. v3 also evaluates CD under additive measurement noise, multiplicative measurement noise, and temporal perturbations. The underlying P12, Danish CD, and GossipCop datasets remain; the stale mortality heading in Appendix F does not establish an additional retained mortality experiment.

E2.justification: For CD, v3 removes Random Forest, Naive Bayes, and Gradient Boosting, retains Transformer and Trans-mean, and adds GRU-D, SeFT, mTAND, DGM2, MTGNN, and Raindrop. The corresponding P12 comparison drops IP-Net. The four GossipCop comparators remain unchanged. This substantially revises comparator membership within the existing medical evaluations.

E3.justification: Medical evaluation switches from AUROC to AUPRC. Appendix F reports a shared 100-epoch setup instead of v1’s task-specific maxima of 300, 500, and 400 epochs, with revised batch sizes, regularization, and architecture search ranges. v3 also introduces calibration and clean-training/noisy-testing protocols. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds five CD component ablations testing DeepSet aggregation, learned distance weighting, and alternatives to ExtGNAN, including standard GNAN. Appendix G adds calibration assessment and controlled additive, multiplicative, and temporal-noise robustness tests. These substantially extend v1’s node/subset attribution analyses, which are largely retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark means and standard deviations over three seeds or runs. v3 additionally specifies that calibration ECE uncertainty is calculated over three data splits. This is limited additional repetition information, not evidence of increased benchmark run counts; no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: v1’s medical AUROC results of 76.64 ± 1.2 for P12 and 83.64 ± 0.9 for CD are replaced by AUPRC results of 97.41 ± 0.38 for ICU length of stay and 83.93 ± 0.27 for CD. Different targets, metrics, and settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains. v3 Tables 3–8 add ablation, grouping, calibration, and robustness results. GossipCop accuracy remains 97.34 ± 0.2, with unchanged comparator scores.

T1.justification: The XOR-based expressivity proofs and four-point recoverability argument are retained from v1 Section 6 in v3 Appendix B. v3 adds a reachability-conditioned distance definition and Appendix C’s computational scaling analysis, including O(m K n^2 d_psi) cost and a sparse-masking argument. These are bounded additions rather than replacements of the central theoretical results.

C1.justification: v1’s headline claims of over four AUROC points improvement for mortality prediction and nearly two points for CD are removed. v3 instead claims state-of-the-art ICU length-of-stay and CD prediction and explicitly promotes learning without information loss or imputation. The central interpretability and increased-expressivity contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly interprets the existing perturbation analysis as a quantitative measure of faithfulness by construction, interprets the new ablations as evidence that the components are critical, and discusses calibration as reliability evidence. Its performance discussion also avoids v1’s blanket 'fully interpretable' description. The principal clinical interpretations and grouping-versus-interpretability trade-off remain.

D1.justification: v3 substantially revises reproducibility documentation: it replaces dataset-specific training recipes with a shared recipe, removes embedding-width ranges and separate GossipCop hardware details, and adds CD control-selection details, explicit alternative biomarker-group memberships, and Gaussian perturbation instructions. These include both added and lost information. The statement that code is provided in supplementary material is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds related-work citations to Tipirneni and Reddy (2022) and Labach et al. (2023), while removing citations including Friedman, Ho, and the IP-Net paper. It more explicitly contrasts its multi-level interpretability and arbitrary-graph support with earlier temporal models. The overall positioning around GNAN and irregular-data learning remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming GMAN to SuperMAN and changing the title, v3 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, expands the graph-input explanation, combines the separate medical-task presentations into shared Data/Setup/Results passages, and reorganizes the appendices into lettered sections. These are substantial editorial and structural revisions.

P2.justification: The two medical result tables are merged into a two-task table. v3 adds the ablation, grouping, calibration, and robustness tables and a calibration plot, while Figure 1 gains explicit graph/subset labels and an expanded caption. Figures 2–4 are largely retained with caption and placement changes. The document also adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v1 supported its architectural choices mainly through overall scores and attribution examples. v3’s component ablations, including direct GNAN and aggregation controls, address the important missing evidence about which innovations contribute to performance. Quantified grouping comparisons and controlled noise tests further strengthen assessment of the central design. This constitutes a substantial evidential improvement, although lost dataset-specific implementation detail, inconsistent P12 descriptions, and unclear ECE scaling limit reproducibility and calibration claims. The changed medical scores themselves do not establish improvement across versions.
